analysis: The change set is documentation-only in docs/developer/test.md. It updates the 'Last updated' date, the CI runner description for cluster runtime tests (now 'macOS CI runners', with a link to build.md#ci-runner-routing), and the description of scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. The route test now pins each routed job's lanes, one per provider or cluster shard. It also now says release workflows are kept on literal Blacksmith runners. The earlier claim that the macOS jobs of ci.yml stay on Blacksmith runners is removed. I reviewed the supplied head text at lines 1386-2302. It is surrounding test documentation that was not changed, so I did not treat it as new behavior. No source, workflow, key-handling, attestation, encryption, authorization or prefix-cache code is modified, so none of T-041, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 or TB-012 is affected. The doc says release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners and that routing is default-off, restricted for fork PRs, label-gated, with read-only permissions. Those statements describe tests and do not weaken any control. Nothing in the diff shows that ci.yml macOS jobs are now routed to a dynamic runner plane. That may be a real CI change in other files, which I did not see. A routed runner for PR-triggered jobs would be a CI trust-boundary concern, but release and signing workflows are documented as unrouted. The workflow and routing scripts that implement this were not in the supplied evidence. A reviewer of those files should check that fork PRs and secret-bearing jobs cannot reach routed runners. This doc cannot establish that, and it does not itself create a vulnerability.
